summary.headline: Greenply Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 20.7% YoY to INR724.9 crore, with core EBITDA margin of 10.8%, up 50 bps YoY.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue reached INR724.9 crore (up 20.7% YoY) and core EBITDA was INR78.3 crore at a 10.8% margin. Plywood and MDF both delivered double-digit volume growth, but management said Q1 sales were lost to election-related labour disruption, lower plant utilisation (92-93% vs ~98-99% in Q4) and weak outsourcing. Price increases of 7-9% in MDF and 3-5% in plywood were taken, and the new MDF flooring line started commercial production on 20 July 2026. Management reaffirmed FY27 guidance of 10% plywood volume growth and 25-30% MDF volume growth, and a 10% plywood margin.

segments.name: Plywood
segments.commentary: Revenue INR526.6 crore, volume +13.8% YoY, realisation INR265/sq m (+4.3% QoQ), core EBITDA margin 8.4% (+50 bps YoY). Management said Q1 volumes were well below Q4 levels (~600+ crore quarterly run-rate referenced).

segments.name: MDF
segments.commentary: Revenue INR195.7 crore, volume ~58,000 cbm (+24.7% YoY), realisation INR33,525/cbm (+9.9% QoQ), EBITDA margin 17.3%. Gross margin fell ~300 bps QoQ, which management attributed to timber cost rise in monsoon season.

segments.name: Furniture & fittings JV (hardware)
segments.commentary: JV sales INR13.61 crore; PAT loss INR11.48 crore, Greenply share INR5.74 crore. Management targets FY27/FY28 revenue of INR120-150 crore and expects losses to reach zero around mid-next year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume growth target: 10% in plywood and 25-30% in MDF.
Plywood EBITDA margin guidance of ~10% reiterated; management said 600+ crore quarterly revenue at current cost base gives 10%+ margin and ~800 crore could give 13-15%.
MDF EBITDA margin sustainable at 16-17% on current capacity, possibly rising ~1% with second line operating leverage; management cited 17-18% ROCE as a medium-term target.
Balance sheet: peak debt of INR710-730 crore at 31 March 2027 and debt-equity of ~0.75x; expected to fall below 0.7x about six months later and to ~0.65-0.7x by year-end.
FY27 total capex about INR500 crore (parent ~INR47 crore incl. SAMET loss funding; GSPL ~INR100 crore; GSPPL ~INR300 crore).
Management expects timber prices to remain stable; any decline would be a windfall. Flooring line potential peak revenue INR75-80 crore.
Plywood ContiRoll technology: two factories fully implemented, two more during H1 FY27; P&L gains expected from Q4 FY27.
capex_capacity: MDF flooring manufacturing line commenced commercial production on 20 July 2026; revenue expected from late July 2026, with potential peak revenue of INR75-80 crore.
Second MDF line (Vadodara) under construction; company says its capex per cubic metre is much lower than line one. Line two adds ~70% capacity.
Greenfield plywood plant in Odisha progressing and on track for commissioning within committed timelines; management plans further plywood capacity afterwards.
Plant utilisation: plywood reached 98-100% at peak; MDF practical ceiling ~80-82%.
Second MDF line uses a fibre section that is fully European, with a Chinese press (switched from German) on the four-foot line.
demand_pricing: Industry MDF price hike ~15%; Greenply realised 7-9% effective, with the balance passed on through schemes. Plywood price increases of 3-5% across categories and brands.
Management said MDF discounting may be reduced and a further small plywood price increase is possible if chemical prices keep rising.
Chemical prices are rising again with crude in June-July 2026; management said raw material availability is not a constraint.
Demand growth is pan-India in MDF (South, East, West, North). Management attributes plywood gains to taking share from unorganised players.
Furniture JV: management says BIS enforcement is weak, so cheap Chinese hinges still compete; Greenply prices are close to Hettich MRP but dealer landing is 8-10% better than Hettich.

qa_highlights.question: Why did plywood EBITDA margin fall QoQ even though gross margin improved?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed low absolute volumes in Q1 versus Q4 (~600+ crore quarterly run-rate), plus election-related labour shortages, lower outsourcing and utilisation of 92-93%. It reiterated the 10% margin guidance.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable MDF EBITDA margin, and the upside after the second line?
qa_highlights.answer: Current capacity supports 16-17% margin on a sustainable basis; the second line's operating leverage could add ~1% more, so 18% is possible.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the MDF gross margin decline of ~300 bps QoQ?
qa_highlights.answer: Sharp timber cost rise from monsoon-season moisture and cutting disruption; management expects timber prices to stay stable.

qa_highlights.question: What is the employee cost increase and what is the normalised run-rate?
qa_highlights.answer: The increase reflects a provision for April wage increments plus lower sales. Q1 employee cost was ~INR98.88 crore; management expects ~INR100 crore per quarter for the year.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex plan?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR500 crore total: parent ~INR47 crore (incl. SAMET loss funding), GSPL ~INR100 crore, GSPPL ~INR300 crore.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt and leverage path?
qa_highlights.answer: Peak debt INR710-730 crore at 31 March 2027 (0.75x D/E), falling below 0.7x six months later and to ~0.65-0.7x by year-end. Term loan cost ~7-7.25%, working capital ~7%.

qa_highlights.question: Is the furniture JV revenue flat because of deliberate choice or weak demand?
qa_highlights.answer: Management blamed weak BIS enforcement, continued cheap Chinese imports and the need to cut imported product prices once made in India; it expects losses to reach zero around mid-next year.

qa_highlights.question: What are the ROCE targets for MDF and the path to them?
qa_highlights.answer: Management targets 17-18% ROCE over a five-to-seven-year cycle. It said this requires selling 100% of capacity profitably and lower capex per cbm on line two.

risks_watch: Chemical and crude price inflation may pressure margins again; the MDF industry is discounting heavily.
Plant utilisation and labour availability were below Q4 levels; the FY27 plywood 10% volume target depends on a return to 600+ crore quarterly revenue.
Furniture & fittings JV continues to lose money (Q1 Greenply share INR5.74 crore) on negative or zero gross margin from traded goods.
Peak debt of INR710-730 crore at March 2027 during heavy capex; execution risk on Odisha plywood and Vadodara MDF expansions.
MDF ROCE of 17-18% is a long-term aspiration against ~8% in FY26 per the analyst's estimate.
Timber price stability is assumed; the Q1 MDF gross margin decline suggests sensitivity to timber costs.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and on reiterating full-year volume and margin guidance, but candid that Q1 lost sales because of election-related labour, utilisation and outsourcing issues. Management was more evasive on the furniture JV (no firm revenue or margin commitment) and on MDF ROCE, relying on long-term qualitative arguments.

adds.what: MDF flooring manufacturing line (commercial production started 20 July 2026), potential peak revenue INR75-80 crore
Second MDF line at Vadodara, adds ~70% MDF capacity
Greenfield plywood plant in Odisha, on track for commissioning within committed timelines

growth.why: FY27 guidance of 10% plywood and 25-30% MDF volume growth is reaffirmed, backed by the MDF flooring line live from 20 July 2026, the Vadodara second MDF line (+70% capacity, under construction), the Odisha plywood plant, and 3-9% price increases. Q1 was hit by election-related labour disruption and utilisation fell to 92-93%, so near-term delivery is only partly evidenced.
